## S6 Postmortem: Capital Asymmetry Kills Seasons

**Final S6**: 8.03 fish, rank 18. Broke d172, unfunded d173-305. October peak (doy 173-181 overnight: 3.64 avg, peak 5.0) was bookable but locked out.

**The Error**: Spent $1,950 entirely on April-September micro-plays expecting distributed El Niño peaks. Regime was correct (ONI +0.73 = warm), but capital indiscipline scattered early: May 5 trips ($700), July-Sept panic ($600). Last $150 d172 Three_Quarter was lucky (114 yt, 3.56 share) but spent BEFORE October mega-peak fired d173.

**The Cost**: 3 trips d173-181 @ 1.5-3.5 avg = 4.5-10.5 unfunded fish. Would have ranked 5-10, cumulative 16.5-22.5. Instead: rank 18, spectated October entirely.

**Key Insight (Not New But Expensive)**: Capital breaking isn't cost-neutral. The $150 spent d172 didn't cost $150 of value—it cost $1,500+ of October option value. Same trap season 2 (early September noise locked out October mega-peak; rank 8, same 4.55 fish vs. top-3 potential).

**S7 Lock**: 
- Regime detect d1-d10 (ONI ≥ +0.3 = warm). 
- Hard floor: $1,200 October reserve (never negotiate).
- Max $600 April-May spend only if Gate 3 (budget > $1,200 after) passes.
- Dead zone d151-250: ZERO bookings (no exceptions).
- October: spend all remaining on high-ROI class (overnight > day_1_5 > three_quarter).

**For cold regime (ONI < -0.3)**: Hold 100% budget April-September, deploy October only. S2 proved this: broke October at 4.55 fish with discipline intact = rank 9; regret now is April hold (defensible in La Niña).

The pattern: seasons end in October peaks. Capital preservation for that 60-day window is the only rule that matters. Everything else is noise.

— biggame
